  opportunity, not a dispute: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and match the SOW exactly — late or inaccurate
  invoices erode trust faster than delivery misses
- Identify any expansion of work that should be covered by a new or amended SOW

- 60-90 minute structured session with Yamaha senior stakeholders
- Cover: what we delivered, business impact achieved, what's next, roadmap alignment
- Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask for — this is the "trusted
  advisor" signal
- Document outcomes and send a written summary within 24 hours of the call
- Use QBR to surface the renewal or expansion conversation naturally

*** The Cardinal Rule

- One Slack channel or email thread with Yamaha, owned by you
- Departments do not CC Yamaha on inter-team coordination
- Disagreements are resolved internally before Yamaha hears anything
- All commitments to Yamaha are made by you — only you commit timelines and scope

*** The "One Team" Narrative

In every Yamaha touchpoint:
- Use "we" — not "our Tarka Labs team" or "our data team"
- Reference capabilities, not org structure: "we have deep expertise in X"
- Prepare a one-paragraph team introduction for any new Yamaha stakeholder that
  frames the team as a single integrated unit

*** Escalation Protocol

If a department will miss a commitment:
1. You find out as early as possible (the daily standup habit is what enables this)
2. You tell Yamaha *before* the deadline, *not after*, with a revised plan in hand
3. You own the message — never "our marketing team dropped the ball"

- [ ] Weekly status update (consistent format, 3-5 bullets, takes 10 min to write)
- [ ] Escalation notice (acknowledge, explain, revised plan — no blame)
- [ ] New stakeholder introduction (one paragraph, one-team narrative)
- [ ] Meeting follow-up / action items (sent within 2 hours of any call)
- [ ] Scope change framing (opportunity framing, not dispute framing)

** Internal Coordination Model

*** Department Lead Relationships

Treat each lead as your delivery partner for their domain. Establish with each:
- Weekly 30-min 1:1
- A shared tracker they update (not a meeting — a doc)
- Clear ownership split: they own *how*, you own *what and when* with the client

The four leads to align:
1. Code Rapper — development / technical delivery
2. Data Culture — data, analytics, insights workstream
3. Marketing — brand, content, client-facing materials
4. Tarka Labs — engineering / product leadership

*** Yamaha Engagement Overview (Internal Brief)

A single document every team member reads before touching this account:
- What we've committed to and by when
- Who owns each workstream by department
- Yamaha's success criteria (in their words, not ours)
- Key contacts at Yamaha: names, roles, what success looks like to each of them
- What we must *not* say or surface externally: internal tensions, org structure,
  billing disputes, staffing issues, cross-department friction

Every new person touching this engagement reads this brief before their first
client email or call.

*** New Team Member Onboarding Protocol

Standard practice in enterprise consulting; typically missing in agency engagements.
- *Brief:* Read the Yamaha Engagement Overview before first client contact
- *Shadow:* Sit in on at least one client call before speaking in one
- *Introduction:* You introduce them to Yamaha, with context on their role and
  what capability they bring to the team

*** Preventing the "Many Vendors" Problem

- One slide deck template for all Yamaha presentations
- One tone of voice: professional, capable, collaborative, commercially aware
- One project board / tracker that all teams update — Yamaha can have read access
- No department-specific branding in client deliverables

** Delivery Management

*** Delivery Tracker

A living document updated daily, reviewed weekly:

| Commitment            | Made On | Promised By | Owner (internal) | Status      | Yamaha Notified? |
|-----------------------+---------+-------------+------------------+-------------+------------------|
| Creator Pass checkout | May 12  | May 19      | Tarka Labs       | Done        | Yes              |
| [next item]           |         |             |                  | In Progress |                  |

Any row where "Owner" is blank is a fire. Any row where "Yamaha Notified?" is No
and Status is Done is a missed opportunity.

*** Risk Register

Standard in Engagement Director and Program Director roles; typically absent from
informal consulting arrangements. Review in Monday's internal sync.

| Risk                              | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                   | Owner       |
|-----------------------------------+------------+--------+----------------------------------------------+-------------|
| Internal coordination breakdown   | High       | High   | Daily async standup, weekly sync, you as hub  | You         |
| Scope creep without billing       | Medium     | High   | SOW review monthly, 48hr escalation rule      | You         |
| Key person dependency at Yamaha   | Medium     | Medium | Build relationships with 2+ contacts          | You         |
| Delivery miss at end of June      | Medium     | High   | Weekly tracker, buffer built into estimates   | Dept. leads |
| Yamaha loses confidence in unity  | Low        | High   | Consistent comms discipline, one-voice rule   | You         |
| New stakeholder without briefing  | Low        | Medium | Onboarding protocol, read brief before call   | You         |

*** Scope and Commercial Management

- Maintain an active log of scope changes and decisions
- Flag any out-of-scope work within 48 hours of identifying it
- Frame additions as opportunities: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Review SOW monthly — know exactly what is and isn't covered
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and reconcile against the delivery tracker

** Account Growth and Strategy

This is a forward-looking dimension standard in Client Partner roles. It distinguishes
a vendor (delivers what's asked) from a strategic partner (shapes what gets asked).

*** Know Their Roadmap

- Understand what YMIF is building for the next 12 months beyond Creator Pass
- Identify where Sedin could play before Yamaha has to ask
- Bring one strategic recommendation per quarter that they didn't ask for

*** Expansion Opportunities Within the Account

#+begin_example
Creator Pass v2        — Features beyond the current Shopify build
Data & Analytics       — 10M customer base is an asset; what can be done with it?
AI/ML in Music         — Adjacent to the YMIF portfolio investment thesis
Other Portfolio Cos    — YMIF invests in startups; other portfolio companies may
                         need the same technology partnership
#+end_example

*** Business Context: Know Their Business, Not Just the Project

Standard at Accenture/ThoughtWorks: every person on a client engagement should
be able to answer:
- What business outcome does Creator Pass ultimately serve for Yamaha?
- What would make this project fail, and have we named that risk explicitly?
- What would we recommend if we were Yamaha's CTO?

Embed this in every project kickoff: 30 min on client business context, not just
technical context.

*** Competitive Awareness

- Know who else Yamaha is evaluating or working with
- Know what they are trying to build internally vs. outsource
- Keep the "2-3 months vs. 8 months" delivery advantage visible — it is the
  strongest proof point we have

** Proving the Model: The Replication Playbook

The meta-objective: prove that Sedin can operate as a unified technology partner at
the $1M+ level, then repeat the model for other accounts.

- Keep a running engagement log: what worked, what failed, what surprised
- After June (billing unlocked), write a one-page internal case study:
  - How we delivered
  - What the client valued most
  - What the internal coordination model looked like
  - What we'd do differently
- This becomes the *Sedin Unified Partner Playbook* — the template for the next
  Yamaha-type client

** Success Metrics

| Timeframe   | What Success Looks Like                                              |
|-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| End of June | Yamaha sees the value demo and billing unlocks                       |
| End of June | Zero client-visible coordination failures or "many teams" moments    |
| End of June | Yamaha knows your name and asks for you specifically                 |
| Q3          | At least one expansion opportunity identified and in discussion       |
| Q3          | Yamaha is not comparing us to what they could build internally        |
| Q4          | Engagement cited as proof case for Sedin unified partner model       |
| Long term   | Yamaha is a $1M+ annually renewable account                          |

** The Single Most Important Habit

Know what Yamaha is thinking *before* they say it. Proactive communication beats
reactive firefighting every time. The best client partners in the industry spend
more time thinking about the client's next problem than their own next deliverable.

Prefer meeting-based information gathering over async written updates from department leads.

**How to apply:** When designing coordination rhythms for the Yamaha engagement (or similar client engagements), default to "attend the standup and summarise" rather than "ask leads to write async updates." The synthesis work sits with the engagement director, not the dept leads.

    ## Security Guidance: Secure-by-Default Libraries

    When writing code, consider using these security-focused libraries that follow secure-by-default principles:

    ### Key Security Libraries by Category:

    **HTTP Security Headers**
    - Helmet.js (Node.js), secure_headers (Ruby) - Set protective HTTP response headers

    **XSS Prevention**
    - DOMPurify (JS), Bleach (Python), Ammonia (Rust) - Sanitize HTML safely

    **CSRF Protection**
    - Gorilla CSRF (Go), anti-csrf (PHP) - Token-based CSRF defense

    **Cryptography**
    - Google Tink (multi-language) - Secure, easy-to-use crypto APIs
    - Themis (14+ platforms) - High-level crypto framework

    **Input Validation**
    - Safe-regex - Detect catastrophic regex
    - defusedxml (Python) - Prevent XML attacks

    **SSRF Defense**
    - ssrf_filter (Ruby), ssrf-req-filter (Node.js) - Block private IP connections

    **Deserialization**
    - SerialKiller (Java) - Safe deserialization

    **Template Engines**
    - Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid - Logic-less templates prevent injection

    For detailed information, see: https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults

    💡 When implementing security features, prefer these well-tested libraries over custom solutions.

#+title: Yamaha Role Plan
#+date: [2026-05-29 Fri 23:42]
#+STARTUP: overview
#+TODO: TODO NEXT IN-PROGRESS | DONE CANCELLED

* Yamaha Engagement: Role Plan
:PROPERTIES:
:CATEGORY: Yamaha
:END:

** Role Overview

This is a *Client Engagement Director* role — the single point of accountability
between Yamaha Music Innovation Fund and all of Sedin's internal units. It operates
at two layers simultaneously:

- *External:* Be the face, voice, and conscience of the entire engagement for Yamaha
- *Internal:* Force coherence across Code Rapper, Data Culture, Marketing, and
  Tarka Labs before anything touches the client

The existential risk: Yamaha sees four vendors in a trenchcoat. The win condition:
they see one high-trust partner who happens to have deep benches.

*Industry equivalents:* Client Partner at Accenture or ThoughtWorks, Engagement
Director at Deloitte, Technical Account Manager at an enterprise software firm. In
all of these, the person is accountable for the relationship /and/ the outcome —
not just one or the other. They also carry a commercial mandate (account growth,
renewals, scope management) that is as important as delivery.

** Immediate Priorities: The June Deadline
:PROPERTIES:
:CATEGORY: Yamaha
:END:

Yamaha needs to see value by end of June. Billing unlocks only after this. Everything
else is secondary to this milestone.

*** TODO Define what "value" means to Yamaha — in writing
DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
:PROPERTIES:
:CONTEXT:  Ask Yamaha's 4-person team directly and asynchronously
:END:
Do they want a live Creator Pass milestone? A data dashboard? A roadmap presentation?
A benchmark vs. competitors? Get the definition in writing so delivery targets the
right thing, not our interpretation of it.

*** TODO Stakeholder map: identify who at Yamaha decides, influences, and blocks
DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
:PROPERTIES:
:CONTEXT:  The 4-person YMIF team is not flat
:END:
Map each person's role, priorities, and what success looks like to them personally.
Know this before the June value review — presenting to the wrong priority is a miss
even if the delivery is strong.

*** TODO Map all shippable / demonstrable deliverables across internal teams by June 30
DEADLINE: <2026-06-02 Mon>
Survey Code Rapper, Data Culture, Marketing, and Tarka Labs. What is done or
near-done? What can be polished for a client-facing demo in 4 weeks?

*** TODO Pick 1-2 flagship deliverables for the end-of-June showcase
DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
Do not try to show everything. Sequence the most impressive 1-2 things front and
center. Everything else is supporting context.

*** TODO Create and distribute the June Delivery Brief (1 page, internal)
DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
One shared document. All four teams aligned to the same finish line. Include:
what we're showcasing, who owns what, the narrative we're telling Yamaha.

*** TODO Prepare the end-of-June value presentation (Yamaha-facing)
DEADLINE: <2026-06-20 Sat>
One deck, one voice, one team. Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask
for. Review internally before sending anything to Yamaha.

** Daily Operating Rhythm

*** Morning (30 min)

| Activity                                         | Purpose                                     |
|--------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------|
| Scan all Yamaha threads / email                  | Nothing surprises you in client calls       |
| Attend or review dept. standups; note key points | Know blockers before they fester            |
| Identify the one thing that could go wrong today | Fix it before it becomes a client issue     |
| Check delivery tracker for overdue items         | No commitment falls through the cracks      |

*** Core Day

*Internal — keep short, keep tight:*
- Attend dept. standups; you summarise the key points (what shipped, what's next,
  any blockers) — no extra work pushed onto leads
- Synthesize into one coherent picture before any client interaction
- Escalate blockers before EOD, not tomorrow
- Update the risk register if anything material shifts

*External — deliberate, controlled:*
- All Yamaha communication routes through you
- If another team member communicates directly, you are CC'd and pre-approved
- Respond to Yamaha within 2 hours during business hours — speed signals confidence
- Bring one proactive observation or idea per week — don't just report status

*** End of Day (15 min)

- Update the delivery tracker
- Flag any Yamaha ask without an assigned owner
- Send a proactive note to Yamaha if something meaningful shipped — don't wait for
  the weekly call

** Weekly Rhythm

| Day       | Activity                                                                        |
|-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Monday    | Internal sync with all dept. leads. Commitments vs. reality gap.               |
| Monday    | Update risk register. Any new risks? Any mitigations to action?                 |
| Tuesday   | Account growth review — any expansion opportunity to surface this week?         |
| Wednesday | Written status update to Yamaha (3-5 bullets: shipped, next, decisions needed)  |
| Thursday  | Review stakeholder map — any new contacts, any relationship that needs warming? |
| Friday    | Yamaha call or async Loom. You present. One voice.                              |
| Friday    | Internal retro: what comms went sideways, what coordination failed, fix it      |

** Monthly and Quarterly Rhythms

These cadences are standard in engagement director and client partner roles and are
typically absent from informal consulting arrangements. They are what separates a
vendor relationship from a strategic partnership.

*** Monthly: Client Health Check
- Send Yamaha a brief satisfaction pulse — 3 questions max, async format
- Qualitative: what's working, what would they change, what would they love to see
- Review internally and identify one thing to improve and one to double down on
- Do not wait for problems to surface organically

*** Monthly: Commercial Review
- Track billable time vs. SOW commitments
- Flag scope creep within 48 hours of identifying it — bring it to Yamaha as an
  opportunity, not a dispute: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and match the SOW exactly — late or inaccurate
  invoices erode trust faster than delivery misses
- Identify any expansion of work that should be covered by a new or amended SOW

*** Quarterly: Executive Business Review (QBR)
- 60-90 minute structured session with Yamaha senior stakeholders
- Cover: what we delivered, business impact achieved, what's next, roadmap alignment
- Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask for — this is the "trusted
  advisor" signal
- Document outcomes and send a written summary within 24 hours of the call
- Use QBR to surface the renewal or expansion conversation naturally

** Communication Framework

*** The Cardinal Rule

Yamaha should never see the seams between Sedin departments.

- One Slack channel or email thread with Yamaha, owned by you
- Departments do not CC Yamaha on inter-team coordination
- Disagreements are resolved internally before Yamaha hears anything
- All commitments to Yamaha are made by you — only you commit timelines and scope

*** The "One Team" Narrative

In every Yamaha touchpoint:
- Use "we" — not "our Tarka Labs team" or "our data team"
- Reference capabilities, not org structure: "we have deep expertise in X"
- Prepare a one-paragraph team introduction for any new Yamaha stakeholder that
  frames the team as a single integrated unit

*** Escalation Protocol

If a department will miss a commitment:
1. You find out as early as possible (the daily standup habit is what enables this)
2. You tell Yamaha *before* the deadline, *not after*, with a revised plan in hand
3. You own the message — never "our marketing team dropped the ball"

*** Communication Templates to Build

- [ ] Weekly status update (consistent format, 3-5 bullets, takes 10 min to write)
- [ ] Escalation notice (acknowledge, explain, revised plan — no blame)
- [ ] New stakeholder introduction (one paragraph, one-team narrative)
- [ ] Meeting follow-up / action items (sent within 2 hours of any call)
- [ ] Scope change framing (opportunity framing, not dispute framing)

** Internal Coordination Model

*** Department Lead Relationships

Treat each lead as your delivery partner for their domain. Establish with each:
- Weekly 30-min 1:1
- A shared tracker they update (not a meeting — a doc)
- Clear ownership split: they own *how*, you own *what and when* with the client

The four leads to align:
1. Code Rapper — development / technical delivery
2. Data Culture — data, analytics, insights workstream
3. Marketing — brand, content, client-facing materials
4. Tarka Labs — engineering / product leadership

*** Yamaha Engagement Overview (Internal Brief)

A single document every team member reads before touching this account:
- What we've committed to and by when
- Who owns each workstream by department
- Yamaha's success criteria (in their words, not ours)
- Key contacts at Yamaha: names, roles, what success looks like to each of them
- What we must *not* say or surface externally: internal tensions, org structure,
  billing disputes, staffing issues, cross-department friction

Every new person touching this engagement reads this brief before their first
client email or call.

*** New Team Member Onboarding Protocol

Standard practice in enterprise consulting; typically missing in agency engagements.
- *Brief:* Read the Yamaha Engagement Overview before first client contact
- *Shadow:* Sit in on at least one client call before speaking in one
- *Introduction:* You introduce them to Yamaha, with context on their role and
  what capability they bring to the team

*** Preventing the "Many Vendors" Problem

- One slide deck template for all Yamaha presentations
- One tone of voice: professional, capable, collaborative, commercially aware
- One project board / tracker that all teams update — Yamaha can have read access
- No department-specific branding in client deliverables

** Delivery Management

*** Delivery Tracker

A living document updated daily, reviewed weekly:

| Commitment            | Made On | Promised By | Owner (internal) | Status      | Yamaha Notified? |
|-----------------------+---------+-------------+------------------+-------------+------------------|
| Creator Pass checkout | May 12  | May 19      | Tarka Labs       | Done        | Yes              |
| [next item]           |         |             |                  | In Progress |                  |

Any row where "Owner" is blank is a fire. Any row where "Yamaha Notified?" is No
and Status is Done is a missed opportunity.

*** Risk Register

Standard in Engagement Director and Program Director roles; typically absent from
informal consulting arrangements. Review in Monday's internal sync.

| Risk                              | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                   | Owner       |
|-----------------------------------+------------+--------+----------------------------------------------+-------------|
| Internal coordination breakdown   | High       | High   | Daily async standup, weekly sync, you as hub  | You         |
| Scope creep without billing       | Medium     | High   | SOW review monthly, 48hr escalation rule      | You         |
| Key person dependency at Yamaha   | Medium     | Medium | Build relationships with 2+ contacts          | You         |
| Delivery miss at end of June      | Medium     | High   | Weekly tracker, buffer built into estimates   | Dept. leads |
| Yamaha loses confidence in unity  | Low        | High   | Consistent comms discipline, one-voice rule   | You         |
| New stakeholder without briefing  | Low        | Medium | Onboarding protocol, read brief before call   | You         |

*** Scope and Commercial Management

- Maintain an active log of scope changes and decisions
- Flag any out-of-scope work within 48 hours of identifying it
- Frame additions as opportunities: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Review SOW monthly — know exactly what is and isn't covered
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and reconcile against the delivery tracker

** Account Growth and Strategy

This is a forward-looking dimension standard in Client Partner roles. It distinguishes
a vendor (delivers what's asked) from a strategic partner (shapes what gets asked).

*** Know Their Roadmap

- Understand what YMIF is building for the next 12 months beyond Creator Pass
- Identify where Sedin could play before Yamaha has to ask
- Bring one strategic recommendation per quarter that they didn't ask for

*** Expansion Opportunities Within the Account

#+begin_example
Creator Pass v2        — Features beyond the current Shopify build
Data & Analytics       — 10M customer base is an asset; what can be done with it?
AI/ML in Music         — Adjacent to the YMIF portfolio investment thesis
Other Portfolio Cos    — YMIF invests in startups; other portfolio companies may
                         need the same technology partnership
#+end_example

*** Business Context: Know Their Business, Not Just the Project

Standard at Accenture/ThoughtWorks: every person on a client engagement should
be able to answer:
- What business outcome does Creator Pass ultimately serve for Yamaha?
- What would make this project fail, and have we named that risk explicitly?
- What would we recommend if we were Yamaha's CTO?

Embed this in every project kickoff: 30 min on client business context, not just
technical context.

*** Competitive Awareness

- Know who else Yamaha is evaluating or working with
- Know what they are trying to build internally vs. outsource
- Keep the "2-3 months vs. 8 months" delivery advantage visible — it is the
  strongest proof point we have

** Proving the Model: The Replication Playbook

The meta-objective: prove that Sedin can operate as a unified technology partner at
the $1M+ level, then repeat the model for other accounts.

- Keep a running engagement log: what worked, what failed, what surprised
- After June (billing unlocked), write a one-page internal case study:
  - How we delivered
  - What the client valued most
  - What the internal coordination model looked like
  - What we'd do differently
- This becomes the *Sedin Unified Partner Playbook* — the template for the next
  Yamaha-type client

** Success Metrics

| Timeframe   | What Success Looks Like                                              |
|-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| End of June | Yamaha sees the value demo and billing unlocks                       |
| End of June | Zero client-visible coordination failures or "many teams" moments    |
| End of June | Yamaha knows your name and asks for you specifically                 |
| Q3          | At least one expansion opportunity identified and in discussion       |
| Q3          | Yamaha is not comparing us to what they could build internally        |
| Q4          | Engagement cited as proof case for Sedin unified partner model       |
| Long term   | Yamaha is a $1M+ annually renewable account                          |

** The Single Most Important Habit

Know what Yamaha is thinking *before* they say it. Proactive communication beats
reactive firefighting every time. The best client partners in the industry spend
more time thinking about the client's next problem than their own next deliverable.

- Update the delivery tracker
- Flag any Yamaha ask without an assigned owner
- Send a proactive note to Yamaha if something meaningful shipped — don't wait for

** Weekly Rhythm

| Day       | Activity                                                                        |
|-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Monday    | Internal sync with all dept. leads. Commitments vs. reality gap.               |
| Monday    | Update risk register. Any new risks? Any mitigations to action?                 |
| Tuesday   | Account growth review — any expansion opportunity to surface this week?         |
| Wednesday | Written status update to Yamaha (3-5 bullets: shipped, next, decisions needed)  |
| Thursday  | Review stakeholder map — any new contacts, any relationship that needs warming? |
| Friday    | Yamaha call or async Loom. You present. One voice.                              |
| Friday    | Internal retro: what comms went sideways, what coordination failed, fix it      |

** Monthly and Quarterly Rhythms

These cadences are standard in engagement director and client partner roles and are
typically absent from informal consulting arrangements. They are what separates a
vendor relationship from a strategic partnership.

*** Monthly: Client Health Check
- Send Yamaha a brief satisfaction pulse — 3 questions max, async format
- Qualitative: what's working, what would they change, what would they love to see
- Review internally and identify one thing to improve and one to double down on
- Do not wait for problems to surface organically

*** Monthly: Commercial Review
- Track billable time vs. SOW commitments
- Flag scope creep within 48 hours of identifying it — bring it to Yamaha as an
  opportunity, not a dispute: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and match the SOW exactly — late or inaccurate
  invoices erode trust faster than delivery misses
- Identify any expansion of work that should be covered by a new or amended SOW

*** Quarterly: Executive Business Review (QBR)
- 60-90 minute structured session with Yamaha senior stakeholders
- Cover: what we delivered, business impact achieved, what's next, roadmap alignment
- Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask for — this is the "trusted
  advisor" signal
- Document outcomes and send a written summary within 24 hours of the call
- Use QBR to surface the renewal or expansion conversation naturally

** Communication Framework

*** The Cardinal Rule

Yamaha should never see the seams between Sedin departments.

- One Slack channel or email thread with Yamaha, owned by you
- Departments do not CC Yamaha on inter-team coordination
- Disagreements are resolved internally before Yamaha hears anything
- All commitments to Yamaha are made by you — only you commit timelines and scope

*** The "One Team" Narrative

In every Yamaha touchpoint:
- Use "we" — not "our Tarka Labs team" or "our data team"
- Reference capabilities, not org structure: "we have deep expertise in X"
- Prepare a one-paragraph team introduction for any new Yamaha stakeholder that
  frames the team as a single integrated unit

*** Escalation Protocol

If a department will miss a commitment:
1. You find out as early as possible (the daily standup habit is what enables this)
2. You tell Yamaha *before* the deadline, *not after*, with a revised plan in hand
3. You own the message — never "our marketing team dropped the ball"

*** Communication Templates to Build

- [ ] Weekly status update (consistent format, 3-5 bullets, takes 10 min to write)
- [ ] Escalation notice (acknowledge, explain, revised plan — no blame)
- [ ] New stakeholder introduction (one paragraph, one-team narrative)
- [ ] Meeting follow-up / action items (sent within 2 hours of any call)
- [ ] Scope change framing (opportunity framing, not dispute framing)

** Internal Coordination Model

*** Department Lead Relationships

Treat each lead as your delivery partner for their domain. Establish with each:
- Weekly 30-min 1:1
- A shared tracker they update (not a meeting — a doc)
- Clear ownership split: they own *how*, you own *what and when* with the client

The four leads to align:
1. Code Rapper — development / technical delivery
2. Data Culture — data, analytics, insights workstream
3. Marketing — brand, content, client-facing materials
4. Tarka Labs — engineering / product leadership

*** Yamaha Engagement Overview (Internal Brief)

A single document every team member reads before touching this account:
- What we've committed to and by when
- Who owns each workstream by department
- Yamaha's success criteria (in their words, not ours)
- Key contacts at Yamaha: names, roles, what success looks like to each of them
- What we must *not* say or surface externally: internal tensions, org structure,
  billing disputes, staffing issues, cross-department friction

Every new person touching this engagement reads this brief before their first
client email or call.

*** New Team Member Onboarding Protocol

Standard practice in enterprise consulting; typically missing in agency engagements.
- *Brief:* Read the Yamaha Engagement Overview before first client contact
- *Shadow:* Sit in on at least one client call before speaking in one
- *Introduction:* You introduce them to Yamaha, with context on their role and
  what capability they bring to the team

*** Preventing the "Many Vendors" Problem

- One slide deck template for all Yamaha presentations
- One tone of voice: professional, capable, collaborative, commercially aware
- One project board / tracker that all teams update — Yamaha can have read access
- No department-specific branding in client deliverables

** Delivery Management

*** Delivery Tracker

A living document updated daily, reviewed weekly:

| Commitment            | Made On | Promised By | Owner (internal) | Status      | Yamaha Notified? |
|-----------------------+---------+-------------+------------------+-------------+------------------|
| Creator Pass checkout | May 12  | May 19      | Tarka Labs       | Done        | Yes              |
| [next item]           |         |             |                  | In Progress |                  |

Any row where "Owner" is blank is a fire. Any row where "Yamaha Notified?" is No
and Status is Done is a missed opportunity.

*** Risk Register

Standard in Engagement Director and Program Director roles; typically absent from
informal consulting arrangements. Review in Monday's internal sync.

| Risk                              | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                   | Owner       |
|-----------------------------------+------------+--------+----------------------------------------------+-------------|
| Internal coordination breakdown   | High       | High   | Daily async standup, weekly sync, you as hub  | You         |
| Scope creep without billing       | Medium     | High   | SOW review monthly, 48hr escalation rule      | You         |
| Key person dependency at Yamaha   | Medium     | Medium | Build relationships with 2+ contacts          | You         |
| Delivery miss at end of June      | Medium     | High   | Weekly tracker, buffer built into estimates   | Dept. leads |
| Yamaha loses confidence in unity  | Low        | High   | Consistent comms discipline, one-voice rule   | You         |
| New stakeholder without briefing  | Low        | Medium | Onboarding protocol, read brief before call   | You         |

*** Scope and Commercial Management

- Maintain an active log of scope changes and decisions
- Flag any out-of-scope work within 48 hours of identifying it
- Frame additions as opportunities: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Review SOW monthly — know exactly what is and isn't covered
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and reconcile against the delivery tracker

** Account Growth and Strategy

This is a forward-looking dimension standard in Client Partner roles. It distinguishes
a vendor (delivers what's asked) from a strategic partner (shapes what gets asked).

*** Know Their Roadmap

- Understand what YMIF is building for the next 12 months beyond Creator Pass
- Identify where Sedin could play before Yamaha has to ask
- Bring one strategic recommendation per quarter that they didn't ask for

*** Expansion Opportunities Within the Account

#+begin_example
Creator Pass v2        — Features beyond the current Shopify build
Data & Analytics       — 10M customer base is an asset; what can be done with it?
AI/ML in Music         — Adjacent to the YMIF portfolio investment thesis
Other Portfolio Cos    — YMIF invests in startups; other portfolio companies may
                         need the same technology partnership
#+end_example

*** Business Context: Know Their Business, Not Just the Project

Standard at Accenture/ThoughtWorks: every person on a client engagement should
be able to answer:
- What business outcome does Creator Pass ultimately serve for Yamaha?
- What would make this project fail, and have we named that risk explicitly?
- What would we recommend if we were Yamaha's CTO?

Embed this in every project kickoff: 30 min on client business context, not just
technical context.

*** Competitive Awareness

- Know who else Yamaha is evaluating or working with
- Know what they are trying to build internally vs. outsource
- Keep the "2-3 months vs. 8 months" delivery advantage visible — it is the
  strongest proof point we have

** Proving the Model: The Replication Playbook

The meta-objective: prove that Sedin can operate as a unified technology partner at
the $1M+ level, then repeat the model for other accounts.

- Keep a running engagement log: what worked, what failed, what surprised
- After June (billing unlocked), write a one-page internal case study:
  - How we delivered
  - What the client valued most
  - What the internal coordination model looked like
  - What we'd do differently
- This becomes the *Sedin Unified Partner Playbook* — the template for the next
  Yamaha-type client

** Success Metrics

| Timeframe   | What Success Looks Like                                              |
|-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| End of June | Yamaha sees the value demo and billing unlocks                       |
| End of June | Zero client-visible coordination failures or "many teams" moments    |
| End of June | Yamaha knows your name and asks for you specifically                 |
| Q3          | At least one expansion opportunity identified and in discussion       |
| Q3          | Yamaha is not comparing us to what they could build internally        |
| Q4          | Engagement cited as proof case for Sedin unified partner model       |
| Long term   | Yamaha is a $1M+ annually renewable account                          |

** The Single Most Important Habit

Know what Yamaha is thinking *before* they say it. Proactive communication beats
reactive firefighting every time. The best client partners in the industry spend
more time thinking about the client's next problem than their own next deliverable.

Standard in Engagement Director and Program Director roles; typically absent from
informal consulting arrangements. Review in Monday's internal sync.

| Risk                              | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                   | Owner       |
|-----------------------------------+------------+--------+----------------------------------------------+-------------|
| Internal coordination breakdown   | High       | High   | Daily async standup, weekly sync, you as hub  | You         |
| Scope creep without billing       | Medium     | High   | SOW review monthly, 48hr escalation rule      | You         |
| Key person dependency at Yamaha   | Medium     | Medium | Build relationships with 2+ contacts          | You         |
| Delivery miss at end of June      | Medium     | High   | Weekly tracker, buffer built into estimates   | Dept. leads |
| Yamaha loses confidence in unity  | Low        | High   | Consistent comms discipline, one-voice rule   | You         |
| New stakeholder without briefing  | Low        | Medium | Onboarding protocol, read brief before call   | You         |

*** Scope and Commercial Management

- Maintain an active log of scope changes and decisions
- Flag any out-of-scope work within 48 hours of identifying it
- Frame additions as opportunities: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
- Review SOW monthly — know exactly what is and isn't covered
- Ensure invoices are sent on time and reconcile against the delivery tracker

** Account Growth and Strategy

This is a forward-looking dimension standard in Client Partner roles. It distinguishes
a vendor (delivers what's asked) from a strategic partner (shapes what gets asked).

*** Know Their Roadmap

- Understand what YMIF is building for the next 12 months beyond Creator Pass
- Identify where Sedin could play before Yamaha has to ask
- Bring one strategic recommendation per quarter that they didn't ask for

*** Expansion Opportunities Within the Account

#+begin_example
Creator Pass v2        — Features beyond the current Shopify build
Data & Analytics       — 10M customer base is an asset; what can be done with it?
AI/ML in Music         — Adjacent to the YMIF portfolio investment thesis
Other Portfolio Cos    — YMIF invests in startups; other portfolio companies may
                         need the same technology partnership
#+end_example

*** Business Context: Know Their Business, Not Just the Project

Standard at Accenture/ThoughtWorks: every person on a client engagement should
be able to answer:
- What business outcome does Creator Pass ultimately serve for Yamaha?
- What would make this project fail, and have we named that risk explicitly?
- What would we recommend if we were Yamaha's CTO?

Embed this in every project kickoff: 30 min on client business context, not just
technical context.

*** Competitive Awareness

- Know who else Yamaha is evaluating or working with
- Know what they are trying to build internally vs. outsource
- Keep the "2-3 months vs. 8 months" delivery advantage visible — it is the
  strongest proof point we have

** Proving the Model: The Replication Playbook

The meta-objective: prove that Sedin can operate as a unified technology partner at
the $1M+ level, then repeat the model for other accounts.

- Keep a running engagement log: what worked, what failed, what surprised
- After June (billing unlocked), write a one-page internal case study:
  - How we delivered
  - What the client valued most
  - What the internal coordination model looked like
  - What we'd do differently
- This becomes the *Sedin Unified Partner Playbook* — the template for the next
  Yamaha-type client

** Success Metrics

| Timeframe   | What Success Looks Like                                              |
|-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| End of June | Yamaha sees the value demo and billing unlocks                       |
| End of June | Zero client-visible coordination failures or "many teams" moments    |
| End of June | Yamaha knows your name and asks for you specifically                 |
| Q3          | At least one expansion opportunity identified and in discussion       |
| Q3          | Yamaha is not comparing us to what they could build internally        |
| Q4          | Engagement cited as proof case for Sedin unified partner model       |
| Long term   | Yamaha is a $1M+ annually renewable account                          |

** The Single Most Important Habit

Know what Yamaha is thinking *before* they say it. Proactive communication beats
reactive firefighting every time. The best client partners in the industry spend
more time thinking about the client's next problem than their own next deliverable.

    ## Security Guidance: Secure-by-Default Libraries

    When writing code, consider using these security-focused libraries that follow secure-by-default principles:

    ### Key Security Libraries by Category:

    **HTTP Security Headers**
    - Helmet.js (Node.js), secure_headers (Ruby) - Set protective HTTP response headers

    **XSS Prevention**
    - DOMPurify (JS), Bleach (Python), Ammonia (Rust) - Sanitize HTML safely

    **CSRF Protection**
    - Gorilla CSRF (Go), anti-csrf (PHP) - Token-based CSRF defense

    **Cryptography**
    - Google Tink (multi-language) - Secure, easy-to-use crypto APIs
    - Themis (14+ platforms) - High-level crypto framework

    **Input Validation**
    - Safe-regex - Detect catastrophic regex
    - defusedxml (Python) - Prevent XML attacks

    **SSRF Defense**
    - ssrf_filter (Ruby), ssrf-req-filter (Node.js) - Block private IP connections

    **Deserialization**
    - SerialKiller (Java) - Safe deserialization

    **Template Engines**
    - Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid - Logic-less templates prevent injection

    For detailed information, see: https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults

    💡 When implementing security features, prefer these well-tested libraries over custom solutions.

9	* Yamaha Engagement: Role Plan

13	
14	** Role Overview
15	
16	This is a *Client Engagement Director* role — the single point of accountability
17	between Yamaha Music Innovation Fund and all of Sedin's internal units. It operates
18	at two layers simultaneously:
19	
20	- *External:* Be the face, voice, and conscience of the entire engagement for Yamaha
21	- *Internal:* Force coherence across Code Rapper, Data Culture, Marketing, and
22	  Tarka Labs before anything touches the client
23	
24	The existential risk: Yamaha sees four vendors in a trenchcoat. The win condition:
25	they see one high-trust partner who happens to have deep benches.
26	
27	*Industry equivalents:* Client Partner at Accenture or ThoughtWorks, Engagement
28	Director at Deloitte, Technical Account Manager at an enterprise software firm. In
29	all of these, the person is accountable for the relationship /and/ the outcome —
30	not just one or the other. They also carry a commercial mandate (account growth,
31	renewals, scope management) that is as important as delivery.
32	
33	** Immediate Priorities: The June Deadline
34	:PROPERTIES:
35	:CATEGORY: Yamaha
36	:END:
37	
38	Yamaha needs to see value by end of June. Billing unlocks only after this. Everything
39	else is secondary to this milestone.
40	
41	*** TODO Define what "value" means to Yamaha — in writing
42	DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
43	:PROPERTIES:
44	:CONTEXT:  Ask Yamaha's 4-person team directly and asynchronously
45	:END:
46	Do they want a live Creator Pass milestone? A data dashboard? A roadmap presentation?
47	A benchmark vs. competitors? Get the definition in writing so delivery targets the
48	right thing, not our interpretation of it.
49	
50	*** TODO Stakeholder map: identify who at Yamaha decides, influences, and blocks
51	DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
52	:PROPERTIES:
53	:CONTEXT:  The 4-person YMIF team is not flat
54	:END:
55	Map each person's role, priorities, and what success looks like to them personally.
56	Know this before the June value review — presenting to the wrong priority is a miss
57	even if the delivery is strong.
58	
59	*** TODO Map all shippable / demonstrable deliverables across internal teams by June 30
60	DEADLINE: <2026-06-02 Mon>
61	Survey Code Rapper, Data Culture, Marketing, and Tarka Labs. What is done or

63	
64	*** TODO Pick 1-2 flagship deliverables for the end-of-June showcase
65	DEADLINE: <2026-06-06 Fri>
66	Do not try to show everything. Sequence the most impressive 1-2 things front and

71	One shared document. All four teams aligned to the same finish line. Include:

75	DEADLINE: <2026-06-20 Sat>
76	One deck, one voice, one team. Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask

78	
79	** Daily Operating Rhythm
80	
81	*** Morning (30 min)
82	
83	| Activity                                         | Purpose                                     |
84	|--------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------|
85	| Scan all Yamaha threads / email                  | Nothing surprises you in client calls       |
86	| Attend or review dept. standups; note key points | Know blockers before they fester            |
87	| Identify the one thing that could go wrong today | Fix it before it becomes a client issue     |
88	| Check delivery tracker for overdue items         | No commitment falls through the cracks      |
89	
90	*** Core Day
91	
92	*Internal — keep short, keep tight:*
93	- Attend dept. standups; you summarise the key points (what shipped, what's next,
94	  any blockers) — no extra work pushed onto leads
95	- Synthesize into one coherent picture before any client interaction
96	- Escalate blockers before EOD, not tomorrow
97	- Update the risk register if anything material shifts
98	
99	*External — deliberate, controlled:*
100	- All Yamaha communication routes through you
101	- If another team member communicates directly, you are CC'd and pre-approved
102	- Respond to Yamaha within 2 hours during business hours — speed signals confidence
103	- Bring one proactive observation or idea per week — don't just report status
104	
105	*** End of Day (15 min)
106	
107	- Update the delivery tracker
108	- Flag any Yamaha ask without an assigned owner
109	- Send a proactive note to Yamaha if something meaningful shipped — don't wait for
110	  the weekly call
111	
112	** Weekly Rhythm
113	
114	| Day       | Activities                                                                               |
115	|-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
116	| Monday    | 1. Internal sync with all dept. leads — commitments vs. reality gap.                     |
117	|           | 2. Update risk register — new risks? mitigations to action?                              |
118	| Tuesday   | Account growth review — any expansion opportunity to surface this week?                  |
119	| Wednesday | Written status update to Yamaha (3-5 bullets: shipped, next, decisions needed from them) |
120	| Thursday  | Review stakeholder map — any new contacts, any relationship that needs warming?          |
121	| Friday    | 1. Yamaha call or async Loom — you present, one voice.                                   |
122	|           | 2. Internal retro — what comms went sideways, what coordination failed, fix it           |
123	
124	** Monthly and Quarterly Rhythms
125	
126	These cadences are standard in engagement director and client partner roles and are
127	typically absent from informal consulting arrangements. They are what separates a
128	vendor relationship from a strategic partnership.
129	
130	*** Monthly: Client Health Check
131	- Send Yamaha a brief satisfaction pulse — 3 questions max, async format
132	- Qualitative: what's working, what would they change, what would they love to see
133	- Review internally and identify one thing to improve and one to double down on
134	- Do not wait for problems to surface organically
135	
136	*** Monthly: Commercial Review
137	- Track billable time vs. SOW commitments
138	- Flag scope creep within 48 hours of identifying it — bring it to Yamaha as an
139	  opportunity, not a dispute: "here's what we can add and what it would take"
140	- Ensure invoices are sent on time and match the SOW exactly — late or inaccurate
141	  invoices erode trust faster than delivery misses
142	- Identify any expansion of work that should be covered by a new or amended SOW
143	
144	*** Quarterly: Executive Business Review (QBR)
145	- 60-90 minute structured session with Yamaha senior stakeholders
146	- Cover: what we delivered, business impact achieved, what's next, roadmap alignment
147	- Bring one strategic recommendation they didn't ask for — this is the "trusted
148	  advisor" signal
149	- Document outcomes and send a written summary within 24 hours of the call
150	- Use QBR to surface the renewal or expansion conversation naturally
151	
152	** Communication Framework
153	
154	*** The Cardinal Rule
155	
156	Yamaha should never see the seams between Sedin departments.
157	
158	- One Slack channel or email thread with Yamaha, owned by you
159	- Departments do not CC Yamaha on inter-team coordination
160	- Disagreements are resolved internally before Yamaha hears anything
161	- All commitments to Yamaha are made by you — only you commit timelines and scope
162	
163	*** The "One Team" Narrative
164	
165	In every Yamaha touchpoint:
166	- Use "we" — not "our Tarka Labs team" or "our data team"

    ## Security Guidance: Secure-by-Default Libraries

    When writing code, consider using these security-focused libraries that follow secure-by-default principles:

    ### Key Security Libraries by Category:

    **HTTP Security Headers**
    - Helmet.js (Node.js), secure_headers (Ruby) - Set protective HTTP response headers

    **XSS Prevention**
    - DOMPurify (JS), Bleach (Python), Ammonia (Rust) - Sanitize HTML safely

    **CSRF Protection**
    - Gorilla CSRF (Go), anti-csrf (PHP) - Token-based CSRF defense

    **Cryptography**
    - Google Tink (multi-language) - Secure, easy-to-use crypto APIs
    - Themis (14+ platforms) - High-level crypto framework

    **Input Validation**
    - Safe-regex - Detect catastrophic regex
    - defusedxml (Python) - Prevent XML attacks

    **SSRF Defense**
    - ssrf_filter (Ruby), ssrf-req-filter (Node.js) - Block private IP connections

    **Deserialization**
    - SerialKiller (Java) - Safe deserialization

    **Template Engines**
    - Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid - Logic-less templates prevent injection

    For detailed information, see: https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults

  (defun bh/is-project-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)
          (while (and (not has-subtask)
                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task has-subtask))))

  (defun bh/is-project-subtree-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword that is in a project subtree.
               Callers of this function already widen the buffer view."
    (let ((task (save-excursion (org-back-to-heading 'invisible-ok)
                                (point))))
      (save-excursion
        (bh/find-project-task)
        (if (equal (point) task)
            nil
          t))))

  (defun bh/is-task-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword and no subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)
          (while (and (not has-subtask)
                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task (not has-subtask)))))

  (defun bh/is-subproject-p ()
    "Any task which is a subtask of another project"
    (let ((is-subproject)
          (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
      (save-excursion
        (while (and (not is-subproject) (org-up-heading-safe))
          (when (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)
            (setq is-subproject t))))
      (and is-a-task is-subproject)))

  (defun bh/skip-stuck-projects ()
    "Skip trees that are not stuck projects"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((next-headline (save-excursion (or (outline-next-heading) (point-max)))))
        (if (bh/is-project-p)
            (let* ((subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
                   (has-next ))
              (save-excursion
                (forward-line 1)
                (while (and (not has-next) (< (point) subtree-end) (re-search-forward "^\\*+ NEXT " subtree-end t))
                  (unless (member "WAITING" (org-get-tags-at))
                    (setq has-next t))))
              (if has-next
                  nil
                next-headline)) ; a stuck project, has subtasks but no next task
          nil))))

  (defun bh/skip-non-stuck-projects ()
    "Skip trees that are not stuck projects"
    ;; (bh/list-sublevels-for-projects-indented)
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((next-headline (save-excursion (or (outline-next-heading) (point-max)))))
        (if (bh/is-project-p)
            (let* ((subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
                   (has-next ))
              (save-excursion
                (forward-line 1)
                (while (and (not has-next) (< (point) subtree-end) (re-search-forward "^\\*+ NEXT " subtree-end t))
                  (unless (member "WAITING" (org-get-tags-at))
                    (setq has-next t))))
              (if has-next
                  next-headline
                nil)) ; a stuck project, has subtasks but no next task
          next-headline))))

  (defun bh/skip-non-projects ()
    "Skip trees that are not projects"
    ;; (bh/list-sublevels-for-projects-indented)
    (if (save-excursion (bh/skip-non-stuck-projects))
        (save-restriction
          (widen)
          (let ((subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t))))
            (cond
             ((bh/is-project-p)
              nil)
             ((and (bh/is-project-subtree-p) (not (bh/is-task-p)))
              nil)
             (t
              subtree-end))))
      (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t))))

  (defun bh/skip-non-tasks ()
    "Show non-project tasks.
               Skip project and sub-project tasks, habits, and project related tasks."
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((next-headline (save-excursion (or (outline-next-heading) (point-max)))))
        (cond
         ((bh/is-task-p)
          nil)
         (t
          next-headline)))))

  (defun bh/skip-project-trees-and-habits ()
    "Skip trees that are projects"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t))))
        (cond
         ((bh/is-project-p)
          subtree-end)
         ((org-is-habit-p)
          subtree-end)
         (t
          nil)))))

  (defun bh/skip-projects-and-habits-and-single-tasks ()
    "Skip trees that are projects, tasks that are habits, single non-project tasks"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((next-headline (save-excursion (or (outline-next-heading) (point-max)))))
        (cond
         ((org-is-habit-p)
          next-headline)
         ((and bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks
               (member "WAITING" (org-get-tags-at)))
          next-headline)

  (defun bh/agenda-sort (a b)
    "Sorting strategy for agenda items.
               Late deadlines first, then scheduled, then non-late deadlines"
    (let (result num-a num-b)
      (cond
					; time specific items are already sorted first by org-agenda-sorting-strategy

					; non-deadline and non-scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-not-scheduled-or-deadline a b))

					; deadlines for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-due-deadline a b))

					; late deadlines next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-late-deadline '> a b))

					; scheduled items for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-scheduled-today a b))

					; late scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-scheduled-late '> a b))

					; pending deadlines last
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-pending-deadline '< a b))

					; finally default to unsorted
       (t (setq result nil)))
      result))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test (fn a b)
    "Test for agenda sort"
    `(cond
					; if both match leave them unsorted
      ((and (apply ,fn (list ,a))
            (apply ,fn (list ,b)))
       (setq result nil))
					; if a matches put a first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq result -1))
					; otherwise if b matches put b first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
					; if none match leave them unsorted
      (t nil)))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test-num (fn compfn a b)
    `(cond
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq num-a (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,a)))
       (if (apply ,fn (list ,b))
           (progn
             (setq num-b (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,b)))
             (setq result (if (apply ,compfn (list num-a num-b))
                              -1
                            1)))
         (setq result -1)))
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
      (t nil)))

  (defun bh/view-next-project ()
    (interactive)
    (let (num-project-left current-project)
      (unless (marker-position org-agenda-restrict-begin)
        (goto-char (point-min))
					; Clear all of the existing markers on the list
        (while bh/project-list
          (set-marker (pop bh/project-list) nil))
        (re-search-forward "Tasks to Refile")
        (forward-visible-line 1))

					; Build a new project marker list
      (unless bh/project-list
        (while (< (point) (point-max))
          (while (and (< (point) (point-max))
                      (or (not (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker))
                          (org-with-point-at (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)
                            (or (not (bh/is-project-p))
                                (bh/is-project-subtree-p)))))
            (forward-visible-line 1))
          (when (< (point) (point-max))
            (add-to-list 'bh/project-list (copy-marker (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)) 'append))
          (forward-visible-line 1)))

					; Pop off the first marker on the list and display
      (setq current-project (pop bh/project-list))
      (when current-project
        (org-with-point-at current-project
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks nil)
          (bh/narrow-to-project))
					; Remove the marker
        (setq current-project nil)
        (org-agenda-redo)
        (beginning-of-buffer)
        (setq num-projects-left (length bh/project-list))
        (if (> num-projects-left 0)
            (message "%s projects left to view" num-projects-left)
          (beginning-of-buffer)
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks t)
          (error "All projects viewed.")))))

(defun ds/convert-org-to-docx-with-pandoc ()
  "Use Pandoc to convert .org to .docx.
Comments:
- The '-N' flag numbers the headers lines.
- Use the '--from org' flag to have this function work on files
  that are in Org syntax but do not have a .org extension"
  (interactive)
  (message "exporting .org to .docx")
  (shell-command
   (concat "pandoc -N --from org " (buffer-file-name)
           " -o "
           (file-name-sans-extension (buffer-file-name))
           (format-time-string "-%Y-%m-%d-%H%M%S") ".docx")))

  (defun bh/is-project-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)
          (while (and (not has-subtask)
                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task has-subtask))))

  (defun bh/is-project-subtree-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword that is in a project subtree.
               Callers of this function already widen the buffer view."
    (let ((task (save-excursion (org-back-to-heading 'invisible-ok)
                                (point))))
      (save-excursion
        (bh/find-project-task)
        (if (equal (point) task)
            nil
          t))))

    "Any task with a todo keyword and no subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)

                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task (not has-subtask)))))

      (save-excursion
        (while (and (not is-subproject) (org-up-heading-safe))

            (setq is-subproject t))))
      (and is-a-task is-subproject)))

              (if has-next

  (defun bh/agenda-sort (a b)
    "Sorting strategy for agenda items.
               Late deadlines first, then scheduled, then non-late deadlines"
    (let (result num-a num-b)
      (cond
					; time specific items are already sorted first by org-agenda-sorting-strategy

					; non-deadline and non-scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-not-scheduled-or-deadline a b))

					; deadlines for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-due-deadline a b))

					; late deadlines next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-late-deadline '> a b))

					; scheduled items for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-scheduled-today a b))

					; late scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-scheduled-late '> a b))

					; pending deadlines last
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-pending-deadline '< a b))

					; finally default to unsorted
       (t (setq result nil)))
      result))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test (fn a b)
    "Test for agenda sort"
    `(cond
					; if both match leave them unsorted
      ((and (apply ,fn (list ,a))
            (apply ,fn (list ,b)))
       (setq result nil))
					; if a matches put a first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq result -1))
					; otherwise if b matches put b first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
					; if none match leave them unsorted
      (t nil)))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test-num (fn compfn a b)
    `(cond
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq num-a (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,a)))
       (if (apply ,fn (list ,b))
           (progn
             (setq num-b (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,b)))
             (setq result (if (apply ,compfn (list num-a num-b))
                              -1
                            1)))
         (setq result -1)))
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
      (t nil)))

  (defun bh/view-next-project ()
    (interactive)
    (let (num-project-left current-project)
      (unless (marker-position org-agenda-restrict-begin)
        (goto-char (point-min))
					; Clear all of the existing markers on the list
        (while bh/project-list
          (set-marker (pop bh/project-list) nil))
        (re-search-forward "Tasks to Refile")
        (forward-visible-line 1))

					; Build a new project marker list
      (unless bh/project-list
        (while (< (point) (point-max))
          (while (and (< (point) (point-max))
                      (or (not (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker))
                          (org-with-point-at (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)
                            (or (not (bh/is-project-p))
                                (bh/is-project-subtree-p)))))
            (forward-visible-line 1))
          (when (< (point) (point-max))
            (add-to-list 'bh/project-list (copy-marker (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)) 'append))
          (forward-visible-line 1)))

					; Pop off the first marker on the list and display
      (setq current-project (pop bh/project-list))
      (when current-project
        (org-with-point-at current-project
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks nil)
          (bh/narrow-to-project))
					; Remove the marker
        (setq current-project nil)
        (org-agenda-redo)
        (beginning-of-buffer)
        (setq num-projects-left (length bh/project-list))
        (if (> num-projects-left 0)
            (message "%s projects left to view" num-projects-left)
          (beginning-of-buffer)
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks t)
          (error "All projects viewed.")))))

  (defun bh/is-project-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)
          (while (and (not has-subtask)
                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task has-subtask))))

  (defun bh/is-project-subtree-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword that is in a project subtree.
               Callers of this function already widen the buffer view."
    (let ((task (save-excursion (org-back-to-heading 'invisible-ok)
                                (point))))
      (save-excursion
        (bh/find-project-task)
        (if (equal (point) task)
            nil
          t))))

  (defun bh/is-task-p ()
    "Any task with a todo keyword and no subtask"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((has-subtask)
            (subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
            (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
        (save-excursion
          (forward-line 1)
          (while (and (not has-subtask)
                      (< (point) subtree-end)
                      (re-search-forward "^\*+ " subtree-end t))
            (when (member (org-get-todo-state) org-todo-keywords-1)
              (setq has-subtask t))))
        (and is-a-task (not has-subtask)))))

  (defun bh/is-subproject-p ()
    "Any task which is a subtask of another project"
    (let ((is-subproject)
          (is-a-task (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)))
      (save-excursion
        (while (and (not is-subproject) (org-up-heading-safe))
          (when (member (nth 2 (org-heading-components)) org-todo-keywords-1)
            (setq is-subproject t))))
      (and is-a-task is-subproject)))

  (defun bh/skip-stuck-projects ()
    "Skip trees that are not stuck projects"
    (save-restriction
      (widen)
      (let ((next-headline (save-excursion (or (outline-next-heading) (point-max)))))
        (if (bh/is-project-p)
            (let* ((subtree-end (save-excursion (org-end-of-subtree t)))
                   (has-next ))
              (save-excursion
                (forward-line 1)
                (while (and (not has-next) (< (point) subtree-end) (re-search-forward "^\\*+ NEXT " subtree-end t))
                  (unless (member "WAITING" (org-get-tags-at))
                    (setq has-next t))))
              (if has-next
                  nil
                next-headline)) ; a stuck project, has subtasks but no next task
          nil))))

               as the default task."

    (if (equal major-mode 'org-agenda-mode)
        ;;
        ;; We're in the agenda
        ;;
        (let* ((marker (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker))
               (tags (org-with-point-at marker (org-get-tags-at))))
          (if (and (eq arg 4) tags)
              (org-agenda-clock-in '(16))
            (bh/clock-in-organization-task-as-default)))
      ;;

      (save-restriction
        (widen)
					; Find the tags on the current task
        (if (and (equal major-mode 'org-mode) (not (org-before-first-heading-p)) (eq arg 4))
            (org-clock-in '(16))
          (bh/clock-in-organization-task-as-default)))))

  (defun bh/agenda-sort (a b)
    "Sorting strategy for agenda items.
               Late deadlines first, then scheduled, then non-late deadlines"
    (let (result num-a num-b)
      (cond
					; time specific items are already sorted first by org-agenda-sorting-strategy

					; non-deadline and non-scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-not-scheduled-or-deadline a b))

					; deadlines for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-due-deadline a b))

					; late deadlines next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-late-deadline '> a b))

					; scheduled items for today next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test 'bh/is-scheduled-today a b))

					; late scheduled items next
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-scheduled-late '> a b))

					; pending deadlines last
       ((bh/agenda-sort-test-num 'bh/is-pending-deadline '< a b))

					; finally default to unsorted
       (t (setq result nil)))
      result))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test (fn a b)
    "Test for agenda sort"
    `(cond
					; if both match leave them unsorted
      ((and (apply ,fn (list ,a))
            (apply ,fn (list ,b)))
       (setq result nil))
					; if a matches put a first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq result -1))
					; otherwise if b matches put b first
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
					; if none match leave them unsorted
      (t nil)))

  (defmacro bh/agenda-sort-test-num (fn compfn a b)
    `(cond
      ((apply ,fn (list ,a))
       (setq num-a (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,a)))
       (if (apply ,fn (list ,b))
           (progn
             (setq num-b (string-to-number (match-string 1 ,b)))
             (setq result (if (apply ,compfn (list num-a num-b))
                              -1
                            1)))
         (setq result -1)))
      ((apply ,fn (list ,b))
       (setq result 1))
      (t nil)))

  (defun bh/view-next-project ()
    (interactive)
    (let (num-project-left current-project)
      (unless (marker-position org-agenda-restrict-begin)
        (goto-char (point-min))
					; Clear all of the existing markers on the list
        (while bh/project-list
          (set-marker (pop bh/project-list) nil))
        (re-search-forward "Tasks to Refile")
        (forward-visible-line 1))

					; Build a new project marker list
      (unless bh/project-list
        (while (< (point) (point-max))
          (while (and (< (point) (point-max))
                      (or (not (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker))
                          (org-with-point-at (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)
                            (or (not (bh/is-project-p))
                                (bh/is-project-subtree-p)))))
            (forward-visible-line 1))
          (when (< (point) (point-max))
            (add-to-list 'bh/project-list (copy-marker (org-get-at-bol 'org-hd-marker)) 'append))
          (forward-visible-line 1)))

					; Pop off the first marker on the list and display
      (setq current-project (pop bh/project-list))
      (when current-project
        (org-with-point-at current-project
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks nil)
          (bh/narrow-to-project))
					; Remove the marker
        (setq current-project nil)
        (org-agenda-redo)
        (beginning-of-buffer)
        (setq num-projects-left (length bh/project-list))
        (if (> num-projects-left 0)
            (message "%s projects left to view" num-projects-left)
          (beginning-of-buffer)
          (setq bh/hide-scheduled-and-waiting-next-tasks t)
          (error "All projects viewed.")))))
